identified_files.identified_title: Agnese Portolan Atlas
identified_files.author: Battista Agnese
identified_files.notes: 16th-century portolan atlas from the Library of Congress. Venetian mapmaker Battista Agnese. Beautiful illuminated maritime charts. Pre-industrial cartographic treasure.

identified_files.filename: Voynich Manuscript coding and decoding methods.pdf
identified_files.identified_title: Voynich Manuscript: Coding and Decoding Methods
identified_files.author: Alexander G. Ulyanenkov
identified_files.notes: Scholarly analysis of the Voynich Manuscript's coding methods. References Yale Beinecke MS 408. Botanical illustrations, astronomical charts, unidentified language in cipher.

identified_files.identified_title: The Voynich Manuscript (Beinecke MS 408)
identified_files.author: Anonymous
identified_files.notes: The actual Voynich Manuscript. 102 parchment folios, 225x160mm. Scientific/magical text in unidentified language, in cipher, based on Roman minuscule. Botanical illustrations, astronomical charts, hand coloring. Yale Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library.

identified_files.identified_title: A History of Witches
identified_files.author: Unknown (county)
identified_files.notes: Historical account of witchcraft. Pre-industrial source. Relevant to the Fae Kingdom and European folklore traditions.

identified_files.identified_title: Ancient Alphabets
identified_files.author: Cong...
identified_files.notes: Study of ancient writing systems. Relevant to the Inn's thesis on decoration-as-language (Book of Kells, hieroglyphs, cuneiform).

identified_files.identified_title: Aegyptiaca: Or, Observations on Certain Antiquities of Egypt
identified_files.author: Joseph White
identified_files.notes: Egyptian antiquities observations. Two parts. Connects to the catacombs/ancient civilizations level.

identified_files.identified_title: An Epitome of Astronomy, Including an Account of the Eidouranion, or Transparent Orrery
identified_files.author: William Walker
identified_files.notes: Astronomy overview featuring the eidouranion — a transparent orrery. DIRECTLY relevant to the Inn's orrery (the cosmology level's central instrument). Walker was a lecturer on astronomy.

identified_files.identified_title: A Curious Hieroglyphic...
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Hieroglyphic studies. Pre-Champollion Egyptian script analysis. Connects to catacombs level and Book of Kells decoration-as-language thesis.

identified_files.identified_title: Ahiman Rezon: Or, A Key to the Principles of Freemasonry
identified_files.author: Laurence Dermott
identified_files.notes: The constitution of the Ancient Grand Lodge of England, written by Dermott. Foundational masonic text. The name 'Ahiman Rezon' is itself a mystery — possibly Hebrew for 'Key to a Brother's Secrets.' Directly relevant to Wrought the Celtic Mason and the masonic tradition.

identified_files.identified_title: Arcana Caelestia: The Heavenly Arcana Contained in the Holy Scriptures
identified_files.author: Emanuel Swedenborg
identified_files.notes: Swedenborg's magnum opus. Heavenly mysteries unfolded from Genesis. Foundational hermetic/esoteric text. Directly relevant to the alchemical staircase and hermetic principles.

identified_files.identified_title: The Alchemist, a Comedy
identified_files.author: Ben Jonson
identified_files.notes: Classic Jacobean play satirizing alchemy and charlatans. First performed 1610 by the King's Men. Considered Jonson's best play. The alchemist Subtle and his schemes. Directly relevant to the Staircase's theme.

identified_files.identified_title: The Art of Shadows, or Universal Dialling
identified_files.author: John Good
identified_files.notes: Treatise on sundials and gnomonics. Tables calculated for London latitude (51°30'). The art of shadows = the study of how shadows cast by the sun can measure time and position.

identified_files.identified_title: Astro-Theology: Or, A Demonstration of the Being and Attributes of God, from a Survey of the Heavens
identified_files.author: William Derham
identified_files.notes: Theological astronomy. Derham (1657-1735) argues for God's existence from celestial observation. Illustrated with copper plates. Companion to his Physico-Theology. Directly relevant to the Cosmology level's thesis.

identified_files.identified_title: Arrian's History of the Expedition of Alexander the Great
identified_files.author: Arrian (trans. Rooke)
identified_files.notes: Arrian's Anabasis — the primary source for Alexander the Great's campaigns. Translated from Greek by Rooke with historical, geographical, and critical notes.

identified_files.identified_title: A Trip to the Moon
identified_files.author: McDevitt
identified_files.notes: Early science fiction about a journey to the moon. Public domain. Relevant to the Cosmology level's exploration themes.

identified_files.identified_title: Astro-Theology (Volume 3)
identified_files.author: William Derham
identified_files.notes: Later edition of Derham's Astro-Theology. Survey of the heavens as proof of divine being.

identified_files.identified_title: The Art of Memory: A Treatise Useful for Such as Are to Speak in Publick
identified_files.author: Dass
identified_files.notes: Renaissance memory art treatise. The art of memory = mnemonic systems using spatial architecture. Directly relevant to the Astronomer's Mind Palace concept.

identified_files.identified_title: Conversations on the Plurality of Worlds
identified_files.author: Bernard Le Bovier de Fontenelle
identified_files.notes: Fontenelle's 1686 classic. Early science fiction / popular astronomy. Dialogues about multiple inhabited worlds. INCREDIBLY relevant to the Cosmology level and the Constant's starlight crystal journey between universes.

identified_files.identified_title: Egyptiana
identified_files.author: Smith
identified_files.notes: Egyptian antiquities and artifacts. Connects to the catacombs level.

identified_files.identified_title: Masterpieces of Painting in The Metropolitan Museum of Art
identified_files.author: Metropolitan Museum of Art
identified_files.notes: Collection of masterpiece paintings from the Met. Relevant to the Spiral Gallery's pre-industrial art collection.

identified_files.identified_title: An Universal History, Vol. 8
identified_files.author: Johannes von Müller
identified_files.notes: Volume 8 of the universal history series.

identified_files.identified_title: An Universal History, Vol. 39
identified_files.author: Various
identified_files.notes: Volume 39 of the universal history series.

identified_files.identified_title: An Universal History (multi-volume)
identified_files.author: Johannes von Müller
identified_files.notes: World history from creation to modern times. Multiple volumes in the collection (vols 00, 05, 08, 39). The Inn's archive thesis in book form.

identified_files.identified_title: The American Dispensatory
identified_files.author: John Redman Coxe
identified_files.notes: American pharmacopoeia containing natural history of medicines. Pre-industrial medical reference.

identified_files.identified_title: A History of Inventions, Discoveries, and Origins, Vol. 4
identified_files.author: Johann Beckmann
identified_files.notes: Beckmann (1739-1811) is considered the father of scientific methodology for studying technology history. Covers origins of inventions and discoveries. Directly relevant to the Antikythera mechanism's intellectual lineage.

identified_files.identified_title: Codex Medicamentarius Europaeus
identified_files.author: Alexander Scherer
identified_files.notes: European pharmacopoeia. Materia medica and pharmacy. Pre-industrial medical reference.

identified_files.identified_title: Annals, or History of the World
identified_files.author: Possibly James Ussher
identified_files.notes: Chronological world history. Possibly Ussher's Annals of the World (1658) which dated creation to 4004 BC, or similar work.

identified_files.identified_title: Legends of Montauk
identified_files.author: Ayre
identified_files.notes: Native American folklore from the Montauk people of Long Island. Connects to the Modern Legends shelf and pre-industrial oral traditions.

identified_files.identified_title: A Tour in Germany
identified_files.author: Russell
identified_files.notes: Pre-industrial travel narrative through German states.

identified_files.identified_title: An History of the Earth and Animated Nature, Vol. 6
identified_files.author: Oliver Goldsmith
identified_files.notes: Goldsmith's natural history encyclopedia. 8 volumes with 72 hand-colored plates. Covers zoology, physical geography, animals, birds, fishes, reptiles.

identified_files.identified_title: The Brownie of Bodsbeck, and Other Tales
identified_files.author: James Hogg
identified_files.notes: Scottish supernatural novel set in the Borders, 1685. Features a brownie — a household spirit. Hogg (1770-1835), the 'Ettrick Shepherd.' DIRECTLY relevant to the Inn — the Fizgigs were originally called brownies before redesign. The brownie lore connects to the Inn's domestic spirit tradition.

identified_files.identified_title: An History of the Earth and Animated Nature, Vol. 18
identified_files.author: Oliver Goldsmith
identified_files.notes: Later volume of Goldsmith's natural history. Washington Irving was among the editors of later editions.

identified_files.identified_title: The Antiquary (later edition)
identified_files.author: Walter Scott
identified_files.notes: Different edition of Scott's novel about an amateur antiquary.

identified_files.identified_title: The Antiquary
identified_files.author: Walter Scott
identified_files.notes: Third of the Waverley novels. Centers on an amateur historian/antiquary. Set in Scotland, late 18th century. The novel literally features a character obsessed with ancient artifacts — kindred spirit to the Inn.

identified_files.identified_title: Ancient Reliques: Or, Delineations of Monastic, Castellated & Domestic Architecture
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Engravings of ancient monastic, castle, and domestic architecture. Directly relevant to the Inn's visual design and the Spiral Gallery.

identified_files.identified_title: The Antiquities of the Anglo-Saxon Church
identified_files.author: John Lingard
identified_files.notes: History of the Anglo-Saxon church. Church history, Middle Ages. Connects to the catacombs/ancient civilizations level.

identified_files.identified_title: The Antiquarian and Topographical Cabinet, Vol. 10
identified_files.author: James Storer & John Greig
identified_files.notes: Series of elegant views of interesting objects of curiosity in Great Britain. Antiquarian engravings of castles, abbeys, monuments.

identified_files.identified_title: A Northern Summer: Or, Travels Round the Baltic
identified_files.author: Sir John Carr
identified_files.notes: Travel narrative through Denmark, Sweden, Russia, Prussia, and Germany in 1804. Pre-industrial European travel account.

identified_files.identified_title: Alypius of Tagaste: Ancient Greek Musical Notation
identified_files.author: Alypius (ed. Webb)
identified_files.notes: Alypius wrote on ancient Greek music theory and notation. Tagaste was in North Africa (Augustine's hometown). DIRECTLY relevant to the Inn's acoustic architecture and the Mohs-to-frequency stone tone system — ancient musical theory is the foundation.

identified_files.identified_title: The Adventures of Sir Launcelot Greaves
identified_files.author: Tobias Smollett
identified_files.notes: A comic novel about a Quixote-like knight wandering the countryside doing good deeds. Arthurian themes in 18th century setting. Relevant to Camelot zone.

identified_files.identified_title: An Universal History, Vol. 5
identified_files.author: Various
identified_files.notes: Volume 5 of the universal history series.

identified_files.identified_title: Alciphron, or The Minute Philosopher
identified_files.author: George Berkeley
identified_files.notes: Berkeley's philosophical dialogues. An apology for the Christian religion against free-thinkers. Seven dialogues. Berkeley (1685-1753), Irish philosopher.

identified_files.identified_title: Verona Illustrata (or Compleat History)
identified_files.author: Scipione Maffei
identified_files.notes: Maffei (1675-1755), Italian antiquarian and scholar. Illustrated history of Verona with archaeological and epigraphic studies. Foundational work in modern archaeology.

identified_files.identified_title: A Voyage Round the World
identified_files.author: Sche...
identified_files.notes: Circumnavigation narrative. Pre-industrial global exploration.

identified_files.identified_title: Bishop Burnet's History of His Own Time
identified_files.author: Gilbert Burnet
identified_files.notes: Bishop of Salisbury's firsthand account from the Restoration of Charles II to the Treaty of Utrecht. Major primary source for late 17th/early 18th century England.

identified_files.identified_title: A Voyage to Æthiopia, Made in the Years 1698, 1699, and 1700
identified_files.author: Charles Jacques Poncet
identified_files.notes: Early European exploration of Ethiopia, Abyssinia, Dongola, Sennar. Pre-industrial African exploration narrative. Connects to the world map's African lore pins.

identified_files.identified_title: Archaeologia Britannica
identified_files.author: Edward Lhuyd
identified_files.notes: PIONEERING STUDY OF CELTIC LANGUAGES. Lhuyd (1660-1709) was the first to systematically study and compare Welsh, Breton, Cornish, Irish, Scottish Gaelic, and Manx. Published from Oxford. DIRECTLY relevant to the Book of Kells zone, Celtic masonry tradition, and the Inn's Celtic knotwork aesthetic. This is one of the most important finds in the mystery pile.

identified_files.identified_title: A Tale of a Tub
identified_files.author: Jonathan Swift
identified_files.notes: Swift's first major work. A prose satire defending the Anglican church. Also contains 'The Battle of the Books.' Swift (1667-1745).

identified_files.identified_title: Two Treatises on the Trinity (On the Errors of the Trinity, 7 Books + Dialogues on the Trinity, 2 Books)
identified_files.author: Michael Servetus
identified_files.notes: Servetus (1511-1553) — Spanish theologian, physician, and Renaissance humanist. First European to correctly describe pulmonary circulation. Burned at the stake by Calvin for these very writings. Anti-Trinitarian. One of the most dangerous minds of the Reformation. DIRECTLY relevant to the catacombs level — heretical texts that challenged religious orthodoxy.

identified_files.identified_title: Anastasius: or, Memoirs of a Greek
identified_files.author: Thomas Hope
identified_files.notes: Novel about a Greek man at the close of the 18th century. Thomas Hope (1770-1831) was a Dutch-British art collector and author. The novel was so well-written that Lord Byron reportedly said he wished he had written it.

identified_files.identified_title: An Autumn Near the Rhine: Or, Sketches of Courts, Society, and Scenery in Germany
identified_files.author: Charles Edward Dodd
identified_files.notes: Travel narrative through the German states bordering the Rhine, with a tour in the Taunus Mountains in 1820.

identified_files.identified_title: The Argonautica (Jason and the Golden Fleece)
identified_files.author: Apollonius of Rhodes
identified_files.notes: The epic poem about Jason, the Argonauts, and the quest for the Golden Fleece. Greek mythological epic from the 3rd century BC. Contains the story of Medea. DIRECTLY relevant to the catacombs level's Greek mythology collection.

identified_files.identified_title: The Antiquarian Restaurant (or related antiquarian text)
identified_files.author: Mouls
identified_files.notes: Antiquarian text, possibly about restoration of ancient monuments or buildings.

identified_files.identified_title: A Succinct Account of the History, Manners, and Customs of the Indian Nations
identified_files.author: John Gottlieb Ernestus Heckewelder
identified_files.notes: Moravian missionary's account of Native American nations who inhabited Pennsylvania and neighboring states. Pre-industrial ethnographic record. DIRECTLY relevant to the world map's American lore pins and the Modern Legends shelf.

identified_files.identified_title: A New Pocket Companion for Oxford, Or, Guide Through the University
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Guide to Oxford University. Digitized from Oxford's own library. Pre-industrial university guide.

identified_files.identified_title: A Second Discovery of America (or related Discovery text)
identified_files.author: Brooks
identified_files.notes: Account related to the discovery of America, possibly with ancient American civilization content. Connects to the world map's American lore pins.

identified_files.identified_title: The History of the Union of Great Britain
identified_files.author: Daniel Defoe
identified_files.notes: Defoe (1661-1731) on the union between England and Scotland. The Robinson Crusoe author as political historian.

identified_files.identified_title: A Supplement to the History of the Union
identified_files.author: Daniel Defoe
identified_files.notes: Supplementary papers to Defoe's history of the Anglo-Scottish union, with original documents.

identified_files.identified_title: The Secret History of Europe
identified_files.author: John Oldmixon
identified_files.notes: Oldmixon's polemical secret history of European power politics, focusing on France under Louis XIV. Pre-industrial political expose. The 'secret history' genre was the 18th century equivalent of investigative journalism.

identified_files.identified_title: A New Discovery of a Vast Country in America
identified_files.author: Louis Hennepin
identified_files.notes: Hennepin's account of exploring a vast country in America extending 4000 miles between New France and New Mexico. Rare Book/Special Collections scan. Pre-industrial primary source on American geography and exploration. RELEVANT to the Smithsonian angle — early French explorer's firsthand account of what was actually found in America before narratives were 'corrected.'

identified_files.identified_title: The American Journal of Science and Arts
identified_files.author: Benjamin Silliman (ed.)
identified_files.notes: Founded 1818 at Yale by Benjamin Silliman. Oldest continuously published scientific journal in the United States. Devoted to geology and related sciences. Pre-industrial American scientific record. RELEVANT to the Smithsonian angle — Silliman's journal published early American archaeological and geological finds before institutional suppression.

identified_files.identified_title: A History of the United States
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Early American history. Pre-industrial account of the United States — relevant to the Smithsonian-suppression angle as this was written before institutional gatekeeping of American archaeological narratives.

identified_files.identified_title: The Antiquarian Itinerary: Comprising Specimens of Architecture, Monastic, Castellated, and Domestic
identified_files.author: James Storer
identified_files.notes: Antiquarian engravings of British architecture — monastic, castle, and domestic. Vestiges of antiquity in Great Britain. DIRECTLY relevant to the Inn's visual design language.

identified_files.identified_title: A Chronological Account of... (Molesworth)
identified_files.author: Robert Molesworth
identified_files.notes: Molesworth (1656-1725) was an Irish politician and diplomat. Known for 'An Account of Denmark' (1694). This appears to be a chronological historical work.

identified_files.identified_title: Anecdotes of the Manners and Customs of London from the Roman Invasion to the Year 1700
identified_files.author: James Peller Malcolm
identified_files.notes: Malcolm (1767-1815), American-born artist who moved to London. Documents London social history from Roman times through 1700. Covers charities, depravities, dresses, amusements.

identified_files.identified_title: A Collection of Epitaphs and Monumental Inscriptions, Historical, Biographical, Literary, and Miscellaneous
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Collection of epitaphs with an essay on epitaphs prefixed. Monumental inscriptions from tombstones. The Inn's archive thesis — preserving words carved in stone.

identified_files.identified_title: Annals of Medicine
identified_files.author: Andrew Duncan
identified_files.notes: Andrew Duncan Sr. (1744-1828), Scottish physician. Annals of Medicine was a pioneering medical journal. Pre-industrial medical record.

identified_files.identified_title: Another Traveller: Or, Cursory Remarks and Critical Observations on a Journey Through Part of the Netherlands
identified_files.author: Samuel Paterson
identified_files.notes: 18th century travel critique through the Netherlands. Pre-industrial European travel account.

identified_files.identified_title: The Antiquities of the Abbey or Cathedral Church of Durham
identified_files.author: Patrick Sanderson
identified_files.notes: Antiquities of Durham Cathedral. Pre-industrial architectural and ecclesiastical history.

identified_files.identified_title: A Collection of Epigrams (1737)
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Collection of epigrams with a critical dissertation on this species of poetry. 18th century literary anthology.

identified_files.identified_title: Ancient and Modern History (Universal History)
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Universal history covering ancient and modern periods. Pre-industrial world history. Part of the Universal History genre that the Inn's archive embodies.

identified_files.identified_title: An English School (Horton)
identified_files.author: Horton
identified_files.notes: Historical text about English schooling. Pre-industrial educational history.

identified_files.identified_title: A Practical Grammar of the Ancient Gaelic, or Language of the Isle of Man (Manks)
identified_files.author: John Kelly
identified_files.notes: Grammar of ancient Gaelic / Manx language. DIRECTLY relevant to Lhuyd's Archaeologia Britannica and the Celtic language tradition. The Isle of Man language is one of the six Celtic languages Lhuyd cataloged. This connects to the Book of Kells zone and the masonry tradition.

identified_files.identified_title: The Book of Nature; or, The True Sense of Things
identified_files.author: William Jones
identified_files.notes: Jones's philosophical work on the true sense of things — nature as text. Natural theology. Pre-industrial philosophical text relevant to the Inn's thesis that decoration is language and nature carries meaning.

identified_files.identified_title: The Ancient Empires (or A History of the Ancient World)
identified_files.author: Philip Smith
identified_files.notes: Philip Smith's ancient history from earliest records to the fall of the Western Empire. Covers Egypt, Assyria, Babylonia, Media, Persia, Greece, Rome. Directly relevant to the catacombs level.

identified_files.identified_title: A Narrative of Extraordinary Operations (Major-General John Campbell in the Hill Tracts of Orissa)
identified_files.author: John Campbell
identified_files.notes: Campbell's account of operations in Orissa for the suppression of human sacrifices and female infanticide. Pre-industrial ethnographic account of Indian hill tribes. Relevant to the world map's Asian lore pins.

identified_files.identified_title: The Ancient History of the East, from the Earliest Times to the Conquest by Alexander the Great
identified_files.author: Philip Smith
identified_files.notes: Ancient history of the East including Egypt, Assyria, Babylonia, Media, Persia. Pre-industrial scholarship on Eastern civilizations. Catacombs level.

identified_files.identified_title: Ancient Jerusalem (Kitt and/or related archaeological study)
identified_files.author: Kitt
identified_files.notes: Study of ancient Jerusalem. Pre-industrial archaeological/biblical scholarship. Catacombs level.

identified_files.identified_title: Original Cantos (by Steele)
identified_files.author: Steele
identified_files.notes: Original poetic cantos. Possibly by Sir Richard Steele (1672-1729), Irish writer and politician, co-founder of The Tatler and The Spectator.

identified_files.identified_title: To Be Continued (Annals/Unit, 1700s)
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Possibly continuation of annals or historical records. Pre-industrial historical text.

identified_files.identified_title: A Key to the First Chart of the Masonic Lodge (or related masonic chart)
identified_files.author: Parmelee (or similar)
identified_files.notes: Masonic explanatory chart key. The 'first chart' likely refers to the Tracing Board used in Masonic lodges to illustrate symbolism. Connects to the staircase (alchemy/transitional) level and the Inn's masonry tradition.

identified_files.identified_title: The Universal Magazine of Knowledge and Pleasure
identified_files.author: J. Hinton (publisher)
identified_files.notes: London-published monthly magazine covering news, letters, debates, poetry, music, biography, and state of learning in Europe. Pre-industrial periodical — the Inn's archive as it appeared in real time.

identified_files.identified_title: The History of Arianism
identified_files.author: Louis Maimbourg (trans. William Webster)
identified_files.notes: History of the Arian controversy — the theological dispute over whether Christ was co-eternal with God the Father. Maimbourg (1610-1686) was a French Jesuit historian. Connects to Servetus (already identified) — both are anti-Trinitarian/heretical texts. Catacombs level.

identified_files.identified_title: Miscellanea Curiosa: Containing a Collection of Some of the Principal Phaenomena in Nature
identified_files.author: Various (Royal Society affiliated)
identified_files.notes: Collection of curious travels, voyages, antiquities, and natural phenomena accounted for by the greatest philosophers. Early Royal Society-adjacent scientific miscellany. Pre-industrial natural philosophy.

identified_files.identified_title: Roman Forgeries, or, A True Account of False Records Discovering the Impostures and Counterfeit Antiquities of the Church of Rome
identified_files.author: A faithful son of the Church of England
identified_files.notes: 1673 attack on Catholic Church forgeries — exposing fabricated relics, false documents, and counterfeit antiquities. Rare Book/Special Collections scan. DIRECTLY relevant to the Inn's thesis about suppressed/rewritten history. The 17th century version of 'who destroyed what to rewrite history.'

identified_files.identified_title: Unknown — possibly a modern document (2009)
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Cannot identify from filename. Appears to be a modern (2009) document, possibly not part of the pre-industrial archive.

identified_files.filename: The Free Mason examind; or, The world brought out of -- by Alexander Slade -- ( WeLib.org ).pdf
identified_files.identified_title: The Free Mason Examined; or, The World Brought Out of Darkness
identified_files.author: Alexander Slade
identified_files.notes: Masonic exposure text — revealing Masonic rituals and secrets. Slade's work was part of the 18th century wave of anti-Masonic and Masonic-exposure literature. Connects to the staircase level and the Candid Disquisition (Calcott) also identified.

identified_files.identified_title: Memoirs of the Connecticut Academy of Arts and Sciences
identified_files.author: Connecticut Academy of Arts and Sciences
identified_files.notes: Early American scientific academy proceedings. Connecticut Academy was one of the first scientific societies in America. Pre-industrial American scientific record.

identified_files.identified_title: Memoirs of the Connecticut Academy of Arts and Sciences (vol. 4-5)
identified_files.author: Connecticut Academy of Arts and Sciences
identified_files.notes: Later volumes of the Connecticut Academy memoirs. American scientific proceedings.

identified_files.identified_title: Unknown — non-standard filename

identified_files.identified_title: Unknown — numeric filename
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Cannot identify from filename. Numeric ID suggests a database export or modern catalog number.

identified_files.identified_title: A Textbook on the Domesday Book
identified_files.author: Morgan
identified_files.notes: Textbook on the Domesday Book — the 1086 survey of England ordered by William the Conqueror. Connects to Maitland's 'Domesday Book and Beyond' (also identified). The Domesday Book is the original 'archive thesis' — a complete national survey recorded in a single book.

identified_files.identified_title: The Case of Opposition Stated Between the Craftsman and the People
identified_files.author: Nicholas Amhurst
identified_files.notes: Amhurst's political pamphlet about opposition politics. Amhurst (1697-1742) was a controversial political writer and satirist. Pre-industrial political discourse.

identified_files.identified_title: Unknown — numeric/catalog filename (vol. 2)
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Cannot identify from filename. Appears to be a Wellcome Library or similar medical heritage scan (b-number catalog).

identified_files.identified_title: The Universal Formula (Griffin, 1850)
identified_files.author: Griffin
identified_files.notes: Medical or scientific formula book from 1850. Possibly a pharmacological or alchemical 'universal formula' reference. Connects to the Codex Medicamentarius and American Dispensatory already identified.

identified_files.identified_title: A Table Alphabeticall (or similar early dictionary/alphabet work)
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Early alphabetical reference work. Possibly related to Cawdrey's 'Table Alphabeticall' (1604), the first English dictionary. Pre-industrial language reference.

identified_files.identified_title: Bravo of Bohemia (or History of Bohemia)
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Historical work about Bohemia (Czech lands). Bohemia was a major center of alchemy, Renaissance science, and esoteric traditions — Rudolf II's court in Prague was a center of alchemical research. Connects to the staircase level.

identified_files.identified_title: A Tract or Treatise (Chronological, 1700s)
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Chronological tract or treatise. Pre-industrial religious or historical text.

identified_files.identified_title: A Bookseller's Catalogue (vol. 2)
identified_files.author: Unknown (bookseller)
identified_files.notes: Antiquarian bookseller's catalogue. A catalogue of catalogues — meta-archival. The Inn's library cataloging impulse in its earliest form.

identified_files.identified_title: A Collection of Arms and Armour (Richardson or similar)
identified_files.author: Richardson (or similar)
identified_files.notes: Collection documenting arms and armour. Pre-industrial military material culture. Relevant to the Spiral Gallery's visual archive.

identified_files.identified_title: An Introduction to... (Bonn, 1700s)
identified_files.author: Unknown
identified_files.notes: Introduction text, possibly related to the University of Bonn or German educational material.

identified_files.identified_title: Beauchamp; Or, the Wheel of Fortune (a Novel)
identified_files.author: James Holroyd Fielding
identified_files.notes: Four-volume novel about fortune's wheel. Fielding (not Henry Fielding — a different author using the name). Pre-industrial literary work.

identified_files.identified_title: A Statement and Circular (Aaron Burr)
identified_files.author: Aaron Burr
identified_files.notes: Political statement by Aaron Burr (1756-1836), third Vice President of the United States. Pre-industrial American political document.

identified_files.identified_title: A Law Grammar; or, Rudiments of the Law
identified_files.author: Giles Jacob
identified_files.notes: Jacob (1686-1744) was a major legal writer. This is a concise grammar of English law. Pre-industrial legal reference.

identified_files.identified_title: A Dissertation on... (Frederic William Maitland)
identified_files.author: Frederic William Maitland
identified_files.notes: Maitland (1850-1906) was the greatest English legal historian. Connects to the Domesday Book studies. 'Domesday Book and Beyond' is his most famous work — this could be that or a related dissertation.

identified_files.identified_title: British Synonymy; or, An Attempt at Regulating the Choice of Words in Familiar Conversation
identified_files.author: Hester Lynch Piozzi
identified_files.notes: Piozzi (1741-1821) was Hester Thrale, Dr. Johnson's close friend and literary companion. Her work on British synonymy was one of the earliest works on English word choice and nuance. Pre-industrial linguistics by one of the most remarkable women of the 18th century.

identified_files.identified_title: An Attempt to Prove... (Ashdown)

identified_files.identified_title: A New Guide to the English Tongue
identified_files.author: Thomas Dilworth
identified_files.notes: Dilworth's famous spelling book and English guide. One of the most widely-used English textbooks in the 18th century, especially in America. Pre-industrial language education.

identified_files.identified_title: Archaeologia Cornu-Britannica; or, An Essay to Preserve the Ancient Cornish Language
identified_files.author: William Pryce
identified_files.notes: MASSIVE FIND. Pryce's 1790 work preserving the ancient Cornish language — the THIRD Celtic language text in the collection. Now we have Lhuyd (Welsh/Breton/Cornish/Irish/Gaelic/Manx comparative), Kelly (Manx grammar), Pryce (Cornish), AND Richards (English-Welsh dictionary). The Book of Kells zone has a complete Celtic language reference library. Cornish was already nearly dead by 1790 — this is a preservation text for a dying language.

identified_files.identified_title: A New History of the Grecian States, from Their Earliest Period to Their Extinction by the Ottomans
identified_files.author: R. Johnson
identified_files.notes: History of the Greek states from earliest period to Ottoman conquest. Pre-industrial Greek history. Catacombs level.

identified_files.author: Wellins Calcott
identified_files.notes: MASSIVE FIND. Calcott's 1769 Masonic treatise — one of the most important early Masonic texts. Explains the principles and practices of Freemasonry. SECOND Masonic text in the collection (after Slade's 'Free Mason Examined'). The staircase (alchemy/transitional) level now has a proper Masonic reference library.
